prompt:
Security report: the Accept-Language header chooses which file the translation loader reads.

get_locale_provider hands the request's Accept-Language header to ProviderFactory.get, which builds a file name from it inside the translations directory. A value such as "../../some/dir/file", or an absolute path without ".json", loads any JSON file the server can read as translations. Every distinct value is also cached in the factory's _store under that value, so each unknown or crafted header adds its own copy of the fallback translations and memory grows without bound.

Expected: ProviderFactory.get(locale) only loads a locale listed in the factory's supported_locales (the <locale>.json files bundled in its directory). Anything else gets the fallback locale's provider and no other file is opened: an unknown name ("asdfadsf"), an absolute path, a "../" traversal, even "../en-US" or "./en-US".
- Providers stay cached in _store, keyed by the bundled locale. get returns the same provider object every time for a locale, and for an unsupported value it returns the very object that get(fallback_locale) returns.
- An unsupported value never becomes a key of _store. After get("en-US") and get("asdfadsf") the keys are exactly {"en-US"}. After get("af-ZA") and get("en-US") they are {"af-ZA", "en-US"}, and those two providers are different objects.
- A key missing from the translations still translates to itself (t("secret") gives "secret").

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/pkgs/i18n` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: fix: restrict i18n locale lookup to bundled translation files (#8759)
